seoTitle: How to Combine Postage on eBay: Flat & Promotional Shipping Rules
metaDescription: Set up combined postage on eBay with flat or promotional shipping rules, so multi-item buyers get discounted shipping automatically at checkout.
intro: Buyers who add three items to their cart and see three separate shipping charges often abandon the order — combined postage fixes that by letting eBay automatically discount or flatten shipping once someone buys more than one item from you. Setting the rule up once in Seller Hub means you never have to manually adjust an invoice again for a multi-item sale. This guide covers exactly where the combined shipping settings live, how the flat shipping rule works, and how to layer on a promotional rule for extra incentive during a sale.

steps.heading: Sign in to your eBay seller account
steps.body: Combined shipping rules are account-level settings, so you need to be signed in to the seller account whose listings you want them applied to, not just browsing eBay as a guest. From the eBay homepage, click Sign in and enter your credentials, or use Continue with Google if that's linked to your account. eBay will remember the account you're switching from if you manage more than one, so double check you're on the right storefront before changing anything — shipping rules apply store-wide, across every active listing.

image.caption: The eBay "Welcome back" sign-in screen for a seller account — combined shipping rules are set per account, so confirm you're on the right one before continuing.

steps.heading: Open Shipping preferences in Seller Hub
steps.body: From My eBay or Seller Hub, look in the left-hand menu for Shipping preferences, usually grouped near Automate feedback and Return preferences under your account settings. eBay uses "Postage preference" and "Shipping preference" interchangeably in different parts of the interface — both point to the same settings area, so don't worry if the wording shifts between pages. This is also where general shipping defaults live, like your handling time and dispatch location, so it's worth a quick look at the rest of the page while you're there.

image.caption: The Shipping preferences area in Seller Hub, with a note clarifying that "Postage Preference" and "Shipping Preference" are the same setting under different names.

steps.heading: Open Combined shipping rules and start a flat rule
steps.body: Inside Shipping preferences, find and click into Combined shipping rules. From there, select Create flat shipping rules, which opens a dialog for setting how postage is charged once a buyer adds more than one item to their order. The dropdown defaults to "Add an amount for each additional item," which is the most common setup: the buyer pays full postage for their first item, then a smaller flat add-on for every item after that, rather than paying full shipping multiple times.

image.caption: The Create flat shipping rules dialog, with the "Add an amount for each additional item" option selected and a profile name field for saving the rule.

steps.heading: Set your per-item amount and save a profile
steps.body: Enter the additional-item charge as a fixed amount — for example, if your standard shipping is $6 and you want each extra item to add only $2, that's what goes in the "Each additional" field. Give the rule a clear Profile name, since you can create multiple shipping profiles for different categories of listings (lightweight items versus bulky ones, for instance) and reuse them later. Click Add profile, then Save, and the rule is stored under Combined shipping rules ready to be applied to your listings.

steps.heading: Add a promotional shipping rule for extra incentive
steps.body: Below the flat shipping rule section sits a separate Promotional shipping rule option, which lets you go further than a flat add-on — for example, offering free shipping on the second item, or a percentage discount once an order crosses a certain value. This is the setting to use during a sale event or clearance push, since it's more aggressive than the standard flat rule and clearly reads as a limited-time offer to buyers browsing your store. Like the flat rule, it's saved as its own profile so you can switch it on and off without rebuilding it each time.

steps.heading: Apply the rule to your listings and test it
steps.body: A saved shipping rule doesn't automatically apply to every listing — check your listing's shipping details or use the bulk edit tool in Seller Hub to assign the correct shipping profile to the items you want covered. Once applied, add two or more of the eligible items to a cart yourself (or ask a trusted buyer to) and walk through checkout to confirm the discounted or flat postage actually calculates correctly before it goes live to real customers. This is the same page eBay flags for exclusions, so review the exclusions list too if certain items shouldn't be part of the combined rate, like oversized or international-only listings.

faq.question: Where do I find combined shipping settings on eBay?
faq.answer: In Seller Hub, open Shipping preferences from the left-hand menu, then click into Combined shipping rules. From there you can create both flat and promotional shipping rules.

faq.question: What's the difference between a flat shipping rule and a promotional one?
faq.answer: A flat rule sets a fixed extra charge per additional item, so shipping scales down predictably as buyers add more to their order. A promotional rule is more aggressive — like free shipping on item two — and is meant for sale periods rather than everyday pricing.

faq.question: Does combined shipping apply automatically to all my listings?
faq.answer: No. You need to assign the saved shipping profile to the specific listings you want it applied to, either individually or through Seller Hub's bulk edit tool.

faq.question: Can I exclude certain items from combined shipping?
faq.answer: Yes — the combined shipping settings include an exclusions option for listings like oversized items or international-only shipping that shouldn't be bundled into the flat or promotional rate.

faq.question: Will combined shipping work for international buyers too?
faq.answer: It can, but international shipping often has different calculated rates by destination, so test a combined order to an international address specifically to confirm the discount applies the way you expect.
